official_sources.title: SF.gov — Learn about rent increases in San Francisco
official_sources.supports: Current 1.6% AGA (3/1/26–2/28/27); once every 12 months; first increase 12 months after lease start; base rent only (includes housing services such as parking/storage, excludes temporary passthroughs/fluctuating charges); no rounding up; 30-day vs 90-day notice (+5 days if mailed); notice contents (dollar, percentage, effective date); percentage in effect on effective date applies; banked increases overview; Rent Increase License (Housing Inventory) required since 7/1/2022 (3/1/2023 for condos and buildings with 1–9 units); no added rent for additional occupant; vacancy decontrol (no limit on initial rent of an emptied unit).

official_sources.title: SF.gov — Current Rates, including Rent Increase, Relocation, Sec. Deposit
official_sources.supports: AGA table 1.6% (26-27) / 1.4% (25-26) / 1.7% (24-25); security deposit interest 4.2% (26-27) / 5.0% (25-26) / 5.2% (24-25); relocation payments 3/1/26–2/28/27: $8,245.00 per tenant, $24,733.00 max per unit, +$5,497.00 elderly/disabled/minor-child households; Ellis Act relocation 3/1/26–2/28/27: $11,110.05 per tenant, $33,330.13 max per unit, +$7,443.90 elderly (62+)/disabled; capital-improvement imputed interest 4.1%/4.3%/4.6%/4.8% for 7/10/15/20-year factors; uncompensated labor rate 6/29/26–present $40.40; Rent Board fees $29.50 (2023-24, 2024-25).

official_sources.title: SF Rent Board Form 571 — Allowable Annual Increases 26-27 (PDF)
official_sources.supports: Complete AGA history 4/1/82–2/28/27 (45 periods incl. footnote: only ONE of the two 1992–93 increases may be imposed).

official_sources.title: SF.gov — Banked rent increases
official_sources.supports: Banking allowed since 4/1/1982; skipped increase bankable only after at least 24 full months pass without any rent increase; banked increases never expire during the tenancy; no cap on banking; not compounded/prorated; add banked percentages and multiply by current base rent; banked increases may be combined with the annual increase; partial use leaves remainder banked; practice carries to new owners but not new tenants; notice must state which part is banked; Rent Increase License required.

official_sources.title: SF.gov — Landlord Petitions and Passthroughs
official_sources.supports: Six petition-based increases require filing BEFORE notice: capital improvement; operating & maintenance; special circumstances (comparable units); Proposition I past-history; utility (petition or worksheet); §1.21 occupancy. Substantial rehabilitation and time extension also petition-based. Bond passthroughs need worksheet, not petition. Petitions free; no charge except possible estimator fee. Increase retroactive to effective date specified in valid notice only if approved. Rent Board address 25 Van Ness Avenue, Suite 700, SF 94102; counselor (415) 252-4600; Mon–Fri 9:00–4:00.

official_sources.title: SF.gov — Find out if San Francisco's rental laws apply to you (archived/redirected page)
official_sources.supports: Full protection (eviction + rent increase limits): most SF residential units, incl. pre-6/13/1979 stock. Partial protection (eviction only, no rent-increase cap): units built after June 13, 1979; most single-family homes and condominiums if tenancy began on/after January 1, 1996; substantially rehabilitated units; some government-regulated units. California Tenant Protection Act may still apply where SF law does not; Rent Board cannot enforce state law. NOTE: this SF.gov path now redirects to an archived page; content preserved in current Rent Ordinance coverage guidance — flagged in methodology.

official_sources.title: SF.gov news — Annual Rent Increase for 3/1/26 - 2/28/27 Announced (January 14, 2026)
official_sources.supports: Official announcement: 1.6% AGA effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027; example $2,000 × .016 = $32.00; also confirms prior 1.4% (3/1/25–2/28/26).

official_sources.title: SF.gov — Rent Board Housing Inventory FAQ
official_sources.supports: Mechanics of the Housing Inventory registration underlying the Rent Increase License (required before imposing annual allowable and/or banked increases; effective July 1, 2022; March 1, 2023 for condominiums and buildings with 1–9 residential units). Not independently read this session — the license requirement itself is verified via S-01 and S-04.

official_sources.title: SF Administrative Code Chapter 37 §37.3 (Rent Limitations) — official code library (American Legal Publishing)
official_sources.supports: Licensed landlord may impose an annual increase not exceeding 60% of the published CPI increase; in no event greater than 7%. License tied to §37.15 reporting (Housing Inventory).

official_sources.title: SF.gov — Evictions in San Francisco
official_sources.supports: Eviction requirements apply to most SF residential units incl. single-family, condos, post-1979 stock; Rent Board counseling 415-252-4600; Rent Board referral listing; rental assistance via SF Service Guide / 311.

official_sources.title: SF Rent Board Form 1007 — Notice to Tenant Required by Rent Ordinance §37.9(c)
official_sources.supports: Official form stating tenants receiving a termination notice are eligible for free assistance through the Tenant Right to Counsel Program; intake via Eviction Defense Collaborative, (415) 659-9184, legal@evictiondefense.org, 976 Mission Street.

official_sources.title: California Civil Code §827 — Notice of change of terms; rent increases (30/90-day)
official_sources.supports: 30-day written notice for increases ≤10% of the rent charged during the prior 12 months (or combined); 90-day notice if >10% (§827(b)(2)–(3)); service personally or by mail per CCP §1013 (mailed notice adds 5 days); notice operates as part of the lease if tenant remains; notice of change in terms for month-to-month tenancies (30 days, less-than-one-month tenancies tied to term).

official_sources.title: California Civil Code §1947.12 — Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) rent cap
official_sources.supports: Rent may not increase more than 5% + CPI, or 10%, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period (§1947.12(a)(1)); no more than two increments per 12 months (§1947.12(a)(2)); new-tenancy initial rate freely set (§1947.12(b)); EXEMPT: housing subject to local rent/price control MORE restrictive than §1947.12(a) (§1947.12(d)(3)) — i.e., SF rent-controlled units — and new construction within prior 15 years (d)(4); the separate-title single-family/condo exemption (d)(5) does NOT apply where the owner is a REIT, corporation, or LLC.

official_sources.title: California Civil Code §1946.2 — TPA just cause for eviction
official_sources.supports: After 12 months' continuous lawful occupancy, tenancy may not be terminated without just cause stated in a written notice (at-fault or no-fault) (§1946.2(a), (b)). Relevant to any increase that functions as a disguised termination and to the tenant-advocate scrutiny checklist.

official_sources.title: California Civil Code §1954.53 — Costa-Hawkins (vacancy decontrol; initial rental rate)
official_sources.supports: Owner may establish the initial rental rate for a dwelling/unit on a new tenancy (vacancy decontrol), except where prior tenancy terminated by owner notice or other anti-avoidance exceptions (§1954.53(a)(1)–(4)). During an ongoing tenancy, SF AGA limits apply — Costa-Hawkins does not authorize mid-tenancy increases above the AGA.

official_sources.title: California Civil Code §51 — Unruh Civil Rights Act
official_sources.supports: All persons entitled to full and equal accommodations/advantages/facilities/privileges/services in all business establishments; protected bases include sex, race, color, religion, ancestry, national origin, disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, citizenship, primary language, immigration status (§51(b), (e)).

official_sources.title: California Government Code §12955 — FEHA housing discrimination
official_sources.supports: Unlawful to discriminate against or harass any person in housing because of race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information (§12955(a)); retaliation for opposing unlawful practices unlawful (§12955(f)); discriminatory notices/ads unlawful (§12955(c)).

official_sources.title: HUD — Report Housing Discrimination (Fair Housing Act)
official_sources.supports: Fair Housing Act protected classes: race, color, national origin, religion, sex, disability, familial status; retaliation illegal; report online or 1-800-669-9777; San Francisco Regional FHEO Office, One Sansome Street, Suite 1200, San Francisco, CA 94104, (415) 489-6524 (see FHEO contact page).

official_sources.title: HUD USER — Fair Market Rents (40th percentile) dataset page
official_sources.supports: HUD annually estimates FMRs (40th percentile gross rents), effective each October 1 (42 USC 1437f; 24 CFR 888.113); used for voucher payment standards and rent ceilings, NOT as a cap on private rents and NOT proof of market rent for a specific unit. Exact FY2027 San Francisco 2-bedroom FMR could NOT be read from the official page this session — see Flag F-R2 (value left blank).

official_sources.title: Federal Register (HUD) — Fair Market Rents, FY 2027, Docket No. FR-6553-N-03 (published 2026-09-01)
official_sources.supports: FY 2027 FMRs effective October 1, 2026; methodology summary; national non-metropolitan rent $1,014; HUD welcomes reevaluation requests; full area-level documentation on HUDUSER.

official_sources.title: HUD — Contact FHEO Offices (San Francisco Regional FHEO Office)
official_sources.supports: Region IX office: One Sansome Street, Suite 1200, San Francisco, CA 94104; (415) 489-6524; (800) 347-3739.
